evidence_spans.text: scGen accurately models perturbation and infection response of cells across cell types, studies and species.
scGen is able to capture both types of responses after stimulation by IFN-β when any of the cell types in the data is held out during training and subsequently predicted

scGen shows good performance for early transit-amplifying (TA.early) cells after infection with H. poly and Salmonella (Fig. 3a,b), predicting each condition with high precision (R2all genes = 0.98 and R2all genes = 0.98, respectively).
scGen outperforms linear methods, conditional VAEs, and style transfer GANs in out-of-sample prediction of perturbation response.

limitations.statement: scGen has been trained on relatively small datasets that only reflect subsets of biological and transcriptional variability; a trained model cannot be expected to be predictive beyond the domain of the training data.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
Predictions require realistic error estimates by holding out parts of the data with known ground truth.

methods.description: scGen combines a variational autoencoder (VAE) with latent space vector arithmetics. The VAE encoder maps gene expression to a latent space; the decoder reconstructs expression. Perturbation response is modeled by adding a delta vector (mean difference between perturbed and control latent representations) to the latent representation of a control cell, then decoding. Architecture adapted for scRNA-seq.
